text:
incident-bot: 
ALERT: p99 latency breach detected for `dedicated-pool-3` (region: us-west2).
p95: 420ms (SLO 250ms)  p99: 2.8s (SLO 500ms)  streaming stalls observed: yes
Affected routes: /v1/generate-stream, /v1/chat/stream
Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/dedicated-latency

Maya P (oncall): 
ack-ing. I see customer errors ticking up too. @Alex (CS) can you confirm any external customer impact alerts? :pager:

Alex (CS): 
We have 2 customers on Premium plans reporting chat timeouts. One on us-west2 reported intermittent stalls starting ~1728001100. They see streaming stalls that then recover. No dropped payments.

Jordan L: 
jumping in — initial metric dump: queue depth for pool-3 spiked from 8 -> 260 in ~60s. autoscaler events show scale requests at 1728001205 and 1728001220 but no new nodes attached until 1728001350. Warmup logs show model load time ~18-22s per replica.

Will C: 
logs snippet from autoscaler: 
```
[1728001220] scale_request: replicas=6 -> 10
[1728001221] provision_request_sent
[1728001280] provisioning_delayed: quota_throttle=TRUE
[1728001347] provision_ack: nodes_ready=4
```
Looks like cloud provider throttled capacity provisioning.

Priya R: 
This matches streaming stalls — clients maintain streams but kv-cache is cold when new replicas come up, initial tokens spike latency. p99 dominated by warmup path.

Maya P (oncall): 
Immediate mitigation options: 
1) Manual scale override (force add warm standby replicas in us-west2) — requires infra approval.
2) Route new/resize traffic to fallback model variant (smaller quantized) in the same region.
3) Apply temporary deadline override to allow queued requests to wait for warmups (risk: increased tail latency but fewer errors).
Which is fastest?

Tom I (infra): 
I can push manual scale to add 6 warm replicas in ~90s if we accept spending. I also can enable reserved burst capacity if infra quota allows (need admin).

Jordan L: 
Fallback model is available: `rw-small-quant` compatible with request shapes. Perf: p95 ~ 180ms, p99 ~ 700ms. It supports streaming but has slightly lower answer quality.

Will C: 
Recommend: 1) immediate route 30% of streaming sessions to `rw-small-quant` via routing policy to reduce queue depth; 2) Tom to manual scale + enable warm standby; 3) set deadline override (client_timeout -> 10s) for non-critical tenant traffic.

Maya P (oncall): 
Doing this now. @Jordan L can you create a routing policy and post commands? @Tom I start manual scale. Priya, monitor p99 for both pools. I'll notify CS.

Jordan L: 
Routing policy snippet: 
```
PATCH /routing/policies/dedicated-pool-3
body: {
  "route": [
    {"model":"rw-default","weight":70},
    {"model":"rw-small-quant","weight":30}
  ]
}
```
Applied at 1728001268.

Tom I (infra): 
Manual scale executed: requested +6 replicas at 1728001272. Provider returned partial; 3 came up at 1728001356, 3 more at 1728001478. Warmup progress logs: 
```
1728001360 warmup: load_model(rw-default) 21.3s
1728001380 warmup: KV cache primed for session prefix
```

Priya R: 
Monitoring: after routing change p95 dropped to ~230ms, p99 down from 2.8s -> 950ms in first 2 minutes. Queue depth fell from 260 -> 70 over 300s. Streaming stalls reduced but still visible at tail for long requests.

Alex (CS): 
Update to affected customers: "We mitigated a service-wide capacity spike by routing a portion of traffic to a lower-latency fallback model and scaling up capacity. Some requests may have experienced higher latency during the window. We're monitoring and will follow up."

Maya P (oncall): 
Post-mortem notes to capture: 
- Cause: sudden burst of traffic to dedicated-pool-3 combined with cloud provider quota throttling led to delayed autoscaling and warmup tail latency.
- Contributing: warm model load times (18-22s) + no warm standby buffer for this pool.
- Mitigations taken: temporary routing to fallback, manual scale override, deadline adjustment for non-critical tenants.
- Next actions: reduce warm model load times, add warm standby buffer policy, review provider quota handling in autoscaler (retry/backoff), add proactive burst detection alerting (queue depth rate-of-change).

Will C: 
I opened a ticket to add a "warm-standby" config flag on dedicated pools (link: https://redwood.internal/infra/issue/INC-172800). Also adding autoscaler exponential backoff visibility.

Jordan L: 
Saving logs + flamegraphs. Will push eval comparing `rw-default` vs `rw-small-quant` quality impact for the affected customers.

Maya P (oncall): 
Handoff to next oncall in 30m. Current state: p99 ~ 420ms, streaming stalls rare but keep monitoring for 1h. Escalate if p99 > 700ms for more than 3 consecutive 5m windows.

Tom I (infra): 
Follow-up: requested quota increase from provider; pending approval. If approved, will enable reserved burst cap for pool-3.

Priya R: 
Adding alert: "queue_depth_rate > 50/s for 1m" -> page SRE team and runbook.

Maya P (oncall): 
thx everyone. I'll draft the incident summary and post to #postmortems once consolidated. :white_check_mark:
